# Farming
You have the ability to grow various plants and crops in CrystallEdge!
# Seeds
To start growing plants, you will need seeds. Seeds are typically obtained by [color=yellow]cutting fruits[/color] using a sharp tool.
[color=yellow]Not all plants have seeds[/color]! For example, to grow potatoes, you need to plant the tubers themselves.
# Soil
Different plants may require different types of soil for planting. Also, some types of soil may be more or less effective, affecting the growth rate of the plant.
You can find out how effective the soil type being used is by examining the growing plant.
- Most domesticated crops grow best on [color=yellow]soil beds[/color]. You can create a bed by using dirt blocks on top of soil tiles. - Mushrooms grow best on [color=yellow]Mycelium[/color]. Mycelium seeds can be purchased from the store and placed on the ground. - Wild plants grow effectively right on [color=yellow]grass tiles[/color]. - You can also use a shovel to remove grass, mycelium, and dig up soil.
# Watering
To make a plant grow, it must be [color=yellow]watered[/color]. In the future different plants may require different reagents, but for now it is only water.
Where to get water: - [color=yellow]Rain[/color] fills any open container left under the open sky - wooden barrels, bottles, mugs, vials. - A planted bed drinks rain straight from the sky too, as long as it is not covered. - The old, unfinished water tiles still exist on every map.
Scoop water with a [color=yellow]bucket[/color] and use it on a plant. Examine the plant to see whether it has drunk all its water yet.
# Plant health
A neglected plant will [color=yellow]wither and die[/color]. What kills it is running completely out of [color=yellow]water[/color] - a plant with no water left slowly takes damage, and once it is spent it dies and leaves a [color=yellow]dead husk[/color]. The husk blocks the tile until you clear it away - a couple of hits will do.
Watering a plant in time [color=yellow]heals[/color] it. A recovering plant spends its water and energy on mending itself before growing, so it grows slowly until it is patched up.
- A crop on bare ground with no water dies in roughly [color=yellow]25 minutes[/color]. - On a proper soil bed, or with any watering at all, it recovers and keeps growing. - Trees are far tougher and practically never wither. - Running out of [color=yellow]light[/color] does not kill a plant - it only pauses growth until light returns.
Examine a plant to check its condition.
# Lighting
Most plants require [color=yellow]natural light[/color] to grow. Mushrooms are an exception - they prefer darkness.
